accepted.question_text: For an even integer m, which non-bipartite triangle-free graph with m edges has the largest spectral radius? Equivalently, among all non-bipartite graphs G with m edges and no C_3 subgraph, determine the extremal graph maximizing lambda(G).

evidence.quote: Problem 3 (Zhai and Shu [45], 2022). For even m, what is the extremal graph attaining the maximum spectral radius over all C3-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges?

accepted.question_text: For an even integer m, which non-bipartite graph with m edges, containing neither C_3 nor C_5 as a subgraph, has the maximum spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 4 (Sun and Li [39], 2023). For even m, what is the extremal graph among all {C3, C5}-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges, achieving the maximum spectral radius?

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2 and an even integer m. Among all non-bipartite graphs with m edges that avoid every odd cycle C_3, C_5, ..., C_{2k+1}, which graph has the largest spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 5 (Li, Feng and Peng [19], 2024). For even m, what is the extremal graph attaining the maximum spectral radius over all non-bipartite {C3, C5, . . . , C2k+1}-free graphs with m edges?

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 1. Does there exist an integer N(k) such that every non-bipartite graph G in G(m, {C_3, C_5, ..., C_{2k+1}}) with even m >= N(k) satisfies one of the three exact spectral extremal descriptions in Conjecture 2.11, according to the congruence class of m - (2k - 1) modulo 3?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.11 (Li and Yu [15], 2023). Let k >= 1. There is an integer N(k). Assume that G is a non-bipartite graph in G(m, {C3, C5, . . . , C2k+1}) with even m >= N(k).
Very recently, Lou, Lu and Zhai [31, Theorem 1.4] confirmed Conjecture 2.11 with m >= 30k+45.

accepted.question_text: Fix r >= 1. For all sufficiently large m, must every B_{2,r+1}-free graph G with m edges satisfy lambda(G) <= sqrt(m), with equality only for complete bipartite graphs? Here B_{2,r+1} = K_2 \/ ((r+1)K_1) is the book graph obtained from K_{2,r+1} by adding an edge between the two vertices of degree r+1.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.5 (Zhai, Lin and Shu [44], 2021). For any graph G in G(m, B2,r+1) with m >= m0(r) for large enough m0(r), one has lambda(G) <= sqrt(m). Equality holds if and only if G is a complete bipartite graph.
From Theorem 3.6, one may see Conjecture 3.5 holds for m0(r) >= (12r)^4.

accepted.question_text: For fixed r >= 1 and m edges, which B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph has the largest spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. What is the extremal graph attaining the maximum spectral radius over all B2,r+1-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges?

accepted.question_text: Fix r >= 1 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is a B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph with m edges, is it true that lambda(G) is at most rho(m, r), where rho(m, r) is the largest root of x^3 - x^2 - (m - 1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0, with equality exactly when m == 1 mod r and G is isomorphic to K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.8. Let r >= 1 and m be sufficiently large. If G is a B2,r+1-free non-bipartite graph with size m, then lambda(G) <= rho(m, r), where rho(m, r) is the largest zero of x^3 - x^2 - (m-1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0. Equality holds if and only if m == 1 (mod r) and G ~= K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2. If G has m edges and contains neither C_{2k+1} nor C_{2k+2}, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2, for all sufficiently large m?
accepted.context_brief: Long odd and even cycle conjecture

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.10 (Zhai, Lin and Shu [44], 2021). Let k >= 2 be a fixed integer. If G in G(m, C2k+1) union G(m, C2k+2) and m is sufficiently large, then lambda(G) <= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2.
Consequently, Conjecture 3.10 was also resolved.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2. If G has m edges and contains neither theta_{1,2,2k-1} nor theta_{1,2,2k}, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2, for all sufficiently large m?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.11 ([30]). Let k >= 2 be a fixed integer. If G in G(m, theta1,2,2k-1) union G(m, theta1,2,2k) and m is sufficiently large, then lambda(G) <= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2.
Li, Zhai and Shu [18] solved Conjecture 3.11 for k >= 3 completely.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 3 and write m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k with 1 <= l <= k - 1. Which graph in G(m, theta_{1,2,2k-1}) union G(m, theta_{1,2,2k}) has the largest spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 7 (Liu et al. [27], 2026). For k >= 3, when m + k(k+1)/2 == l (mod k) with 1 <= l <= k - 1, which graphs in G(m, theta1,2,2k-1) union G(m, theta1,2,2k), achieve the largest spectral radius?
By employing k-core analysis combined with spectral techniques, Liu et al. [27] overcomed Problem 7 as follows.

accepted.question_text: For integers q >= p >= 3, what is the maximum spectral radius among graphs in G(m, theta_{1,p,q})? Equivalently, characterize the extremal graphs with m edges that avoid the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q between the same two endpoints.

evidence.quote: Problem 8 (Li, Zhao and Zou [17], 2025). What is the maximum spectral radius of graphs among G(m, theta1,p,q) for q >= p >= 3?
Theorem 3.36 together with Theorem 3.27 solve Problem 8 completely.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is F_{k,3}-free, where F_{k,3} = K_1 \/ kK_2 is the friendship graph made of k triangles sharing a common vertex, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.28 (Li, Lu and Peng [25], 2023). Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be large enough. If G in G(m, Fk,3), then lambda(G) <= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2. Equality holds if and only if G ~= Kk \/ (m/k - (k-1)/2)K1.
Together with Theorems 3.29 and 3.38, Conjecture 3.28 is confirmed.

accepted.question_text: For each t >= 5, what is the maximum spectral radius among all F_t-free graphs with m edges, and which extremal graphs attain that value, where F_t = K_1 \/ P_{t-1} is the fan graph on t vertices?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 (Zhang and Wang [46]). What is the maximum spectral radius and what are the corresponding extremal graphs among all Ft-free graphs with size m for t >= 5?

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.34 (Yu, Li and Peng [42], 2025). Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be sufficiently large. If G in G(m, F2k+1) or G in G(m, F2k+2), then lambda(G) <= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2.
Hence, Conjecture 3.34 follows directly from Theorems 3.32 and 3.35.

accepted.question_text: For integers q >= p >= r >= 2, how can one characterize the graphs in G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) that have the largest spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 10 (Li, Zhao and Zou [17], 2025). How can we characterize the graphs among G(m, thetar,p,q) having the largest spectral radius for q >= p >= r >= 2?
As products of Theorem 3.48, Li, Liu and Zhang [22] solved Problem 7 with a quite different method from that of Liu et al. [27], and solved Problem 10, Conjecture 3.39 completely.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G avoids both theta_{1,p,q} and theta_{1,r,s}, with q >= p >= 3, s >= r >= 3, p + q = 2k + 1, and r + s = 2k + 2, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that graph?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.39. Let k >= 2. There is an m0 such that for all m >= m0, and for all G in G(m, theta1,p,q) union G(m, theta1,r,s) with q >= p >= 3, s >= r >= 3, p + q = 2k + 1 and r + s = 2k + 2.
As products of Theorem 3.48, Li, Liu and Zhang [22] solved Problem 7 with a quite different method from that of Liu et al. [27], and solved Problem 10, Conjecture 3.39 completely.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G is F_{k,3}-free, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that extremal graph?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.40. Let k >= 2. There is an m0 such that for all m >= m0, and for all G in G(m, Fk,3). If m + k(k+1)/2 == l (mod k) with 1 <= l <= k - 1, then lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}). Equality holds if and only if G ~= S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G is F_{2k+2}-free, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that extremal graph?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.41. Let k >= 2. There is an m0 such that for all m >= m0, and for all G in G(m, F2k+2). If m + k(k+1)/2 == l (mod k) with 1 <= l <= k - 1, then lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}). Equality holds if and only if G ~= S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+1}-free, where W_{2k+1} is the odd wheel on 2k+1 vertices, must the extremal graph for lambda(G) depend only on the residue class of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k, taking the complete join K_k \/ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 in the divisible case and S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the other residue classes?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.44. Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be sufficiently large, and G is a W2k+1-free graph with m edges.
Conjecture 3.44 is still open.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G avoids every wheel W_t of order t >= 2k + 1, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.46. Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be sufficiently large. If G in G(m, {Wt : t >= 2k + 1}), then lambda(G) <= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2. Equality holds if and only if G ~= Kk \/ (m/k - (k-1)/2)K1.

accepted.question_text: Let r >= 3 and let G be a K_{r+1}-free graph with m >= r + 1 edges. Must the sum of squares of the two largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy lambda_1(G)^2 + lambda_2(G)^2 <= 2m(1 - 1/r)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 (Bollobas and Nikiforov [2]). Let G be a Kr+1-free graph of size m >= r + 1. Then lambda1^2(G) + lambda2^2(G) <= 2m(1 - 1/r).
Lin, Ning and Wu [26] solved Conjecture 4.2 for r = 2 (see Theorem 2.3), and Conjecture 4.2 is still open for r >= 3.

accepted.question_text: Fix r >= 3 and write m = ar + b with a a non-negative integer and 1 <= b <= r. Among all non-r-partite K_{r+1}-free graphs with m edges, which graph has the largest spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 11 (Lou, Lu and Zhai [31], 2025). For every r >= 3 and every positive integer m = ar + b, where a is a non-negative integer and 1 <= b <= r, what is the extremal graph with maximal spectral radius over all non-r-partite Kr+1-free graphs on m edges?

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 1 and r >= 3. For all sufficiently large m, if G is B_{r,k+1}-free, where B_{r,k+1} = K_r \/ (k+1)K_1 is the generalized book graph, must lambda(G) be at most sqrt(2m(r - 1)/r), with equality only for complete regular r-partite graphs?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 (Li, Liu and Feng [23], 2022). For k >= 1, r >= 3 and sufficiently large m. If G in G(m, Br,k+1), then lambda(G) <= sqrt(2m(r - 1)/r). Equality holds if and only if G is a complete regular r-partite graph.
Li, Liu and Zhang [20] solved Conjecture 4.3 by showing the following result.

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+2}-free, where W_{2k+2} is the even wheel on 2k+2 vertices, must lambda(G) be at most sqrt(4m/3), with equality only for regular complete 3-partite graphs?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.5 (Yu, Li and Peng [42], 2025). Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be large enough. If G in G(m, W2k+2), then lambda(G) <= sqrt(4m/3). Equality holds if and only if G is a regular complete 3-partite graph.
Consequently, Conjectures 4.3 and 4.5 are resolved completely.

accepted.question_text: Given a color-critical graph F with chromatic number chi(F) = r + 1, determine the F-free graphs with m edges that attain the maximum spectral radius.

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Given a color-critical graph F with chi(F) = r + 1, determine the graphs that attain the maximum spectral radius among all F-free graphs with m edges.
Recently, Li, Liu and Zhang [22] solved Problem 12 by showing the following nice result.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Let F be a color-critical graph with chi(F) = r + 1 >= 4. For all sufficiently large m, what is the extremal graph with maximal spectral radius over all non-r-partite F-free graphs on m edges?
